## ForceConnect 2.2 — encrypted DNS that actually connects

ForceConnect 2.2 makes **DNS over HTTPS, TLS and QUIC** work end to end. A small resolver built into the app now runs on your own machine, takes the plain DNS your system sends, and forwards it to your chosen server over the encrypted protocol you picked. 2.2 also adds an **Activity** screen, a **backup server**, and **connect on launch**.

> Already on 2.1.2? This update installs from inside the app: click **Install** when ForceConnect offers it. Coming from 2.1.1 or earlier, install it by hand once, and later updates arrive by themselves after that.

### ✨ What's new

- **Encrypted DNS, for real** — pick DoH, DoT, DoQ or DoH3 and connect. Your system talks to ForceConnect's local resolver on `127.0.0.1` / `::1`, and only encrypted traffic leaves your machine.
- **Encrypted protocols first** — the protocol toggle lists the encrypted protocols first, and DoH is the default.
- **Faster lookups** — answers are cached for as long as their TTL allows, and switching servers happens in place without dropping a single query.
- **Backup server** — choose an encrypted server in **Settings → Backup server**. If your main server fails three times in a row, ForceConnect asks the backup first for the next 30 seconds, so a blocked server doesn't take your internet down with it.
- **Know when something's wrong** — if your server stops answering, you get a warning and a one-click switch to another protocol.
- **Activity screen** — see lookups, cache hits, failures and answers from the backup, browse a live query log, and run a **leak test** to check that your DNS really goes where you think it does.
- **Connect on launch** — turn it on in Settings and ForceConnect reconnects to your last server when it starts.
- **Follows your network** — when traffic moves to another adapter (say, from Wi-Fi to Ethernet), the connection moves with it.
- **Test all is gentler** — it checks at most 8 servers at a time, and now includes your custom servers.
- **Simpler About page** — links in one place.

### 🛠 Fixes

- DNSSEC requests and "no such domain" answers are passed through as they are, instead of turning into errors.
- Another program holding port 53 on all addresses (such as Windows Internet Connection Sharing) no longer stops the resolver from starting.
- **Linux:** the resolver now runs without root. The privileged helper opens port 53 and hands it over.

### 📥 Download

| Platform         | File                                                              | Requirements                                        |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| **Windows**      | `ForceConnect_2.2.0_x64-setup.exe`                                | Windows 10 version 2004 (build 19041) or later, x64 |
| **macOS** (beta) | `ForceConnect_2.2.0_universal.dmg`                                | macOS 10.15 or later, Apple Silicon or Intel        |
| **Linux** (beta) | `.deb` (Debian, Ubuntu), `.rpm` (Fedora, openSUSE) or `.AppImage` | NetworkManager or systemd-resolved, and polkit      |

### ⚠️ Good to know

- **Windows SmartScreen** may warn that the installer is from an unrecognized publisher, because it isn't code-signed yet. Click **More info → Run anyway**.
- **macOS and Linux are still in beta.** On macOS, right-click ForceConnect and choose **Open** the first time you launch it, because the app isn't notarized yet. Please [report how it goes](https://github.com/Mxqius/ForceConnect/issues/new).

### 🐞 Feedback

Found a bug or want a DNS provider added? [Open an issue](https://github.com/Mxqius/ForceConnect/issues). Adding a provider needs no Rust — just edit [`servers.json`](https://github.com/Mxqius/ForceConnect/blob/main/src-tauri/crates/dns/servers.json).
